module purpose: neorv32_spi is a bus-mapped SPI controller with transmit and receive FIFOs. It stores bus-written control settings, queues transmit/control words, generates SPI clock/data/chip-select outputs, captures incoming serial data into the receive path, and raises a configurable interrupt.

use-case flows.value: store SPI enable, phase, polarity, prescaler, divider, highspeed, and interrupt-enable control bits from a bus write to the control register
enqueue a 9-bit transmit/control item into the transmit FIFO and let the transceiver consume it in idle state
generate transfer pacing, advance the transceiver state machine, shift the serial register, sample spi_dat_i, and drive spi_dat_o and spi_clk_o
apply a queued chip-select control word to the external chip-select outputs
generate the interrupt request from the configured FIFO- and busy-related conditions
return control bits, FIFO status, active-chip-select status, busy status, or a received byte on a bus read
clear control state, interrupt output, transceiver state, chip selects, and clock-divider state to known values

conceptual assets.reasoning: The control write stores ctrl.enable at line 140, with GATED_BY records from bus_req_i.stb, bus_req_i.rw, and bus_req_i.addr and a DERIVES_FROM record from bus_req_i.data. This bit directly controls whether both FIFOs are cleared (lines 211 and 243), whether irq_o can assert (line 255), whether the transceiver state bit 2 is set (line 281), whether the clock divider is reset (lines 369-370), and it leaves the entity on clkgen_en_o (line 383). Corrupting it makes these implemented behaviors incorrect, so integrity is established; availability is also established because the bit is stored until rewritten and exported on clkgen_en_o.

The control write stores ctrl.cpha, ctrl.cpol, ctrl.prsc, ctrl.cdiv, and ctrl.highspeed at lines 141-145. These stored settings define serial-clock behavior: ctrl.cpol sets idle/end clock level at lines 286, 320, and 331; ctrl.cpha and ctrl.cpol define active-phase clock values at lines 301, 309, and 324; ctrl.prsc and ctrl.highspeed gate divider progress at line 371; and ctrl.cdiv is compared at line 372 to generate spi_clk_en at line 373. Integrity is established because wrong settings directly change the implemented sampling/driving phase and pacing of transfers. Availability is also established because these settings are held in registers until rewritten.

The control write stores ctrl.irq_rx_avail, ctrl.irq_tx_empty, ctrl.irq_tx_nhalf, and ctrl.irq_idle at lines 146-149. The irq_generator then uses exactly these stored bits in the irq_o formula at lines 255-259 together with rx_fifo.avail, tx_fifo.avail, tx_fifo.half, and rtx_engine.busy. Integrity is established because corrupting any of these stored enables changes which implemented conditions can raise the interrupt. Availability is also established because the bits are held until rewritten.

conceptual assets.concept: Transfer progress state and busy/not-idle decision
conceptual assets.reasoning: The transceiver state register is reset at line 270, loaded with enable in bit 2 at line 281, and advances through transfer phases at lines 293, 303, 312, 322, 325, and 333. The case on rtx_engine.state at line 282 selects whether the engine loads a FIFO item, samples spi_dat_i, shifts rtx_engine.sreg, asserts done, or returns to idle; tx_fifo.re is also generated from state="100" at line 214. The derived busy decision is computed at line 340 from the low state bits and is then used for status reporting at line 172 and for the idle-interrupt condition at line 259. Integrity is established because corrupting this state/decision makes implemented sequencing and busy reporting incorrect; availability is established because state progression is explicitly driven by tx_fifo.avail and spi_clk_en under the coded conditions.

A transmit/control FIFO item is formed on tx_fifo.wdata at line 213. When the transceiver is in state "100" and tx_fifo.avail='1', the command/data tag tx_fifo.rdata(8) is tested at line 289; for a control item, rtx_engine.cs_ctrl is loaded from tx_fifo.rdata(3 downto 0) at line 290. The chip_select process then drives all chip selects inactive at line 352 and, when rtx_engine.cs_ctrl(3)='1', drives one indexed line active at line 354; the active-chip-select status is also reported at line 171. Integrity is established because the external chip-select outputs must match this stored control state; availability is also established because cs_ctrl is retained until changed or reset.

A queued transmit item is formed on tx_fifo.wdata at line 213. In transceiver state "100", when tx_fifo.avail='1' and the command/data tag does not indicate a chip-select command, rtx_engine.sreg is loaded from tx_fifo.rdata(7 downto 0) at line 292 and the state advances at line 293. The current output bit is then driven by spi_dat_o <= rtx_engine.sreg(7) at line 343, and the register shifts during active transfer at line 318. Integrity is established because the SPI output stream must reflect the loaded byte and the implemented shift behavior; availability is established because the byte is held in rtx_engine.sreg and advanced when the enabled transfer clock fires.

The receive path samples spi_dat_i into rtx_engine.sdi_sync at line 310, then shifts the sampled bit into rtx_engine.sreg at line 318. On transfer completion, rx_fifo.wdata is driven from rtx_engine.sreg at line 244 and rx_fifo.we is asserted from rtx_engine.done at line 245 so the assembled byte is delivered to the receive FIFO sub-block. Integrity is established because this is the module-defined receive byte later used by the readout path; availability is established because each completed transfer explicitly presents the assembled byte to the FIFO input.

The serial clock register rtx_engine.sck is assigned from ctrl.cpol in idle/end cases at lines 286, 320, and 331, and from phase/polarity-dependent expressions at lines 301, 309, and 324. The resulting value leaves the entity on spi_clk_o at line 344. Integrity is established because an external SPI peer must receive the clock levels and transitions defined by the coded state/timing rules; availability is established because the register is updated under the implemented transfer conditions and continuously exported.

The irq_generator computes irq_o at lines 255-259 as ctrl.enable AND the selected rx/tx/busy conditions, and resets it to '0' at line 253. This is a module-generated event/report consumed outside the entity, so integrity is established because the output must match that explicit formula; availability is also established because the decision is updated on each rising edge while the module is enabled.
